discovery: Solution of the relativistic two-body problem: effective-one-body theory and numerical relativity simulations of binary black hole mergers

nominees.name: Thibault Damour
nominees.affiliation: Institut des Hautes Etudes Scientifiques (IHES), France

nominees.name: Alessandra Buonanno
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Gravitational Physics (Albert Einstein Institute), Potsdam, Germany

motivation: Every compact-binary detection by LIGO, Virgo and KAGRA, from GW150914 to the roughly 300 events of the GWTC-4 era, depends on accurate waveform models of the inspiral, merger and ringdown. Buonanno and Damour's effective-one-body formalism (1999-2000) gave the first analytic description of the complete coalescence and predicted the waveform's smooth transition from merger to ringdown. Pretorius's 2005 breakthrough in numerical relativity achieved the first stable simulation of the full binary black hole merger in Einstein's theory. Together these results turned general relativity's two-body problem into a working tool. They supply the template banks that matched-filter searches use to find weak signals in noise, and the models used for parameter estimation, population inference and strong-field tests of gravity. Without them, gravitational-wave astronomy could not detect or interpret most of its sources.
